title.narrative: Emergency Health, WASH and Protection response to internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities in Region (R1) with a focus on hard- to- reach communities

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtSince the start of conflict in Sudan in 2023, 998022 IDPs have sought refuge in R1 with the numbers continuing to rise. This has increased the pressure on already scare basic Health and WASH facilities in R1. Additionally, new needs have been created by IDP influx, especially in the newly established IDP camps. R1 faced severe food insecurity in 2024 with 60% population in IPC 3 or above (Multi Sectoral Needs Assessment -MSNA, 2024). The increased population, failed harvest of 2023-2024, steep increase in prices of commodities including food due to Sudan conflict lead to this situation. Access to Protection /GBV services remain skeletal within R1 with a need for augmentation of both protection/GBV services as well as awaress.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThis multi-sector project will provide emergency Health, Protection and WASH services in R1’s Central Region (Umdurein and Tobo counties) and hard-to-reach enclaves of Rashad and New Tagali. P6’s partner, Swiss Global Relief (SGR) will serve a total of 59,285 individuals (17,193M, 18,971W, 11,264B, 11,857G) through its health intervention, delivering essential primary and secondary health care services, including trauma care, emergency obstetric and newborn care (EmONC), and referrals. The project will support four health facilities in Rashad, New Tagali, one health facility in Umdurein, as well as two facilities in Tobo, complemented by three Test and Treat (TnT) points in Tobo and Umdurein during the malaria surge season. Services will focus on treating communicable and non-communicable diseases, reproductive health care, and life-saving referrals to the Mother of Mercy Hospital (MMH) in Gidel, facilitated by two ambulances. To strengthen emergency preparedness, P6’S partner, SGR will improve referral pathways, provide targeted training for health workers on infection prevention and control (IPC), communicable diseases, and primary healthcare unit (PHCU) guidelines, and deploy 16 community health workers to enhance health awareness at the community level. The project will also rehabilitate and upgrade the Agiri health facility to improve security and enhance service delivery.ltbrgtThe Protection intervention aims to enhance prevention and response to GBV with a focus on supporting women and girls who have experienced violence. The project will implement a comprehensive approach that includes the capacity building of healthcare professionals, the provision of case management and psychosocial support, and community engagement to foster sustainable change in attitudes and behaviors related to GBV. The project will target 39,475 individuals (10,060M, 16,505W, 8200G, 4710B) from Tobo and Umdurein counties. ltbrgtThe WASH interventions will improve access to potable drinking water, basic sanitation, and hygiene supplies for 25,350 individuals (13,182 F, 12,168 M) in IDP camps and health facilities in underserved host locations within Tobo/Al-Buram and Umdurein counties, as well as in the enclave areas of Rashad and New Tagali/Abbasiyya. To improve access to water, the project will rehabilitate forty hand pump boreholes, construct hand-dug wells at three supported healthcare facilities in the enclaves of Rashad and New Tagali/Abbasiyya, alongside provision of two hand pump boreholes, benefiting approximately 22,200 individuals. 600 displaced individuals in Tobo/Al-Buram and Umdurein will gain access to basic sanitation through the construction of one hundred household latrines within IDP camps. This project will also include the establishment of three gender-sensitive and disability-inclusive latrines, complete with handwashing facilities, at a supported satellite clinic at a camp in Umdurein, along with a solid waste disposal pit. To promote hygiene and overall well-being, P6’s partner, SGR will provide essential non-food items (NFIs) for five hundred households through this intervention, including hygiene and water storage kits, reaching an estimated 3,000 displaced individuals in Tobo/Al-Buram.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
